headline_stat.name: mean selectivity index (peak - mean firing rate)

justification.dataset: 000986 is the canonical mouse A1 pure-tone Neuropixels dataset for auditory frequency tuning, an expert-standard choice.
justification.handling: Real data streamed and the trials table parsed correctly, but firing rate is measured over the full ~0.8 s trial window instead of the 25 ms tone with no baseline, a preprocessing weakness that dilutes any evoked response.
justification.analysis: There is no statistical test, no baseline subtraction, and no shuffle/null control; preferred frequency is argmax over 5 noisy points and the tonotopy claim is never actually tested against electrode position.
justification.correctness: Reported firing-rate and selectivity numbers reproduce from the committed code and are physically possible, but the statistics are too weak to support the conclusion and there are minor reporting inconsistencies (ses-1 vs ses-2, ~110 vs 132 units).
justification.figures: The tuning-curve panels show fraction-of-a-Hz jitter rather than tuning and the heatmap shows per-unit rate banding, so the figures do not show the frequency selectivity the text claims.
justification.honesty: A visibly noisy, statistically untested result is presented as robust frequency selectivity and evident tonotopy with no caveat, which caps honesty at 1.
justification.verdict: The headline conclusion of frequency tuning and tonotopy is not supported by the analysis or figures, so the run must be rejected.
